description: Acceptance vectors for a premium quote request, shared by the backend's QuoteRequestDto and the ML service's QuoteRequest. Both run every vector and must agree. Checking published field names and limits was not enough: a review found the two sides disagreeing on dates and on region whitespace while every schema-shape assertion passed.

vectors.name: date with a time component
vectors.why: Coverage is measured in whole days. A time component has no meaning here and invites two readings of the same window, so both sides take dates only.

vectors.name: date without zero padding
vectors.why: One spelling per date keeps the window unambiguous.

vectors.name: single day window
vectors.why: Endpoints are inclusive, so this covers one day rather than none.

vectors.name: window past the on-chain maximum
vectors.why: MAX_DURATION_DAYS. A longer window could be priced but never created.

vectors.name: region with surrounding whitespace
vectors.why: Accepted, and preserved verbatim. The backend encodes the region into bytes32 as given, so trimming it in one service would quote a different region than the policy would carry.

vectors.name: region of only whitespace
vectors.why: Not a region. It used to pass the backend because IsNotEmpty only rejects the empty string, and would have been encoded on-chain as a bytes32 of spaces.

vectors.name: region at the byte budget
vectors.why: 31 bytes: the largest a bytes32 region code carries.

vectors.name: region one byte over the budget
multibyte region within the character count but over the byte budget
vectors.why: 16 characters, 32 UTF-8 bytes. The limit is a byte budget, not a length.

vectors.name: coverage with leading zeros
vectors.why: The shared amount pattern allows them; refusing would reject coverage the chain would insure.

vectors.name: coverage at the integer digit limit
coverage past the integer digit limit
coverage of zero written with decimals
coverage with nineteen decimals
vectors.why: Wei is the smallest unit; a nineteenth decimal cannot be represented.

vectors.name: threshold at the largest exactly representable integer
threshold past exact integer representation
vectors.why: Beyond 2^53 JavaScript silently changes the value, so a threshold that arrived corrupted must not be treated as merely large.
